title: quercus cerris var. haliphlaeos
intro:
Quercus cerris var. haliphlaeos, commonly known as the Turkey oak, is a deciduous tree species native to Southeastern Europe and Asia Minor, characterized by its broad leaves and distinctive growth patterns.

Research has shown that the Turkey oak is rich in health benefits, including antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, which may help to protect against chronic diseases such as heart disease and cancer. The therapeutic actions of Turkey oak include its ability to soothe digestive issues, reduce fever, and alleviate respiratory problems. The bioactive constituents of Turkey oak include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
